brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut — they keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% peers, giving clear room to move

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps (market asking band is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% of every ₹100 they sell, while similar firms keep only 3.8% — that 2.1% gap is our room. The market shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume, so a double-digit cut is defensible.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in exchange for part of the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster costs us ₹22.57 L in cash; their borrowing rate is 12.19%, so this is worth roughly that much to them annually — use it to sweeten the price deal

brief.financialLeverage: They are healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, making ₹937.60 Cr revenue and keeping 5.9% profit (well above the 3.8% peer benchmark). But their cash is stuck for 104 days vs 79 days for similar firms, so they feel the pinch on cash flow. We are only 0.59% of their revenue, so we're not critical to them — but their 22.1% growth means they want new orders. Push hard on price (plenty of margin cushion), and dangle faster payment to close the gap.

evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

evidence.point: They already pay their own suppliers slower than peers

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; health score B (65/100); top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue) doing pails, containers, pharma packaging; health score B (73/100); strong and profitable alternate

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — manufacturer, India-Pan presence, medium confidence

risks: They are in the grey zone (Altman Z-score 2.17) — not distress, but not rock-solid either. Don't squeeze so hard they tip over; frame the ask around locking in supply and qualifying a second source.
We spend only ₹5.49 Cr with them (0.59% of their revenue), so we have limited volume leverage — tie any price cut to a volume commitment or faster payment to make it worth their while.

Market asking price verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' with only modest headroom — a 10–15% cut is at the edge of what the market will bear, so be ready to justify it with volume, payment speed, or a multi-year deal.
Their credit rating is strong (CRISIL A+ / Stable), so they won't fold easily — prepare to walk and show the alternates are real.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a three-year deal at a 10–15% better price — you're keeping 5.9% profit vs the industry's 3.8%, and we're ready to pay you faster or commit more volume to get there.
